discovery: Aberration-corrected electron optics enabling sub-ångström transmission electron microscopy

nominees.name: Harald Rose
nominees.affiliation: Ulm University and Technische Universität Darmstadt, Germany

nominees.name: Knut Urban
nominees.affiliation: Forschungszentrum Jülich and RWTH Aachen University, Germany

subfield: Condensed matter physics / electron optics and materials physics
motivation: For decades Scherzer's theorem limited electron microscopes to resolutions far worse than the electron wavelength permits. Rose devised a practicable hexapole corrector for spherical aberration. Haider, Rose and Urban then built it and showed in 1998 that it works, opening sub-ångström imaging. Aberration-corrected TEM and STEM now resolve single atoms, point defects, dislocation cores, solute clusters and interfaces directly. Before, these could only be inferred. In radiation-damage physics this changed the work: we can now test ab initio and molecular-dynamics predictions of defect structures, Cr precipitation in Fe–Cr steels, and fission-gas bubbles in nuclear fuels atom by atom. The impact reaches semiconductors, catalysis, batteries and quantum materials. Few instruments have done as much to change what physicists can measure. This is fundamental physical insight turned into technology used in laboratories worldwide.
